title: Divyanka Tripathi and Vivek Dahiya Brought Their Twin Boys Home. The Internet Watched the Security Guard Bless Them.
excerpt: After a decade of marriage, Indian television's most beloved couple welcomed twin sons. A viral moment with their building's watchman captured why fans have always loved Divyanka.
body:
Of all the moments from Divyanka Tripathi and Vivek Dahiya's journey into parenthood, the one that broke the internet had nothing to do with a hospital or a celebrity post. It was a six-second pause at the entrance of their Mumbai apartment building.

As Divyanka walked in carrying one of her newborn twin sons, wrapped in a white blanket, she stopped at the gate. The building's security guard — an older man the couple's followers have seen in their vlogs over the years — was holding the door open. Divyanka turned, smiled, and showed him the baby. The guard gently touched the infant's head and gave his blessing. The family walked in.

The video, captured by paparazzi, has been viewed millions of times. Comment sections across Instagram and YouTube filled with variations of the same sentiment: "This is why we love her."

## "Mere Karan Arjun Aa Gaye"

The twin boys were born on May 26, 2026, at a hospital in Mumbai, after Divyanka and Vivek had been married for nearly a decade. The couple had announced the pregnancy in March, after keeping it private for six months.

Their birth announcement — a playful illustrated image of two baby boys sitting on clouds in matching blue outfits — carried the message: "We asked for happiness... God said, 'Take double.' Blessed with twin baby boys."

In the caption, Vivek added a line that every Indian viewer immediately recognized: "Mere Karan Arjun aa gaye!" — the iconic dialogue from the 1995 Bollywood classic about a mother reunited with her twin sons. The reference was pitch-perfect and characteristically warm: the couple has always blended humor with genuine emotion in their public communication.

## The Hospital Exit That Went Viral

Three days later, on May 29, Divyanka and Vivek left the hospital with their twins for the first time. The car arriving at the hospital was decorated with blue and white balloons. Vivek, carrying one baby, grinned and told waiting photographers: "Presenting the new mother and father in town."

Divyanka, in white, beamed as she held the other son. Then she made a request to the assembled media: don't photograph the babies' faces.

The press agreed, and the family posed together before heading home. At their residence, Vivek's mother performed a traditional aarti — a welcoming ceremony — for the babies as they entered the house for the first time.

In a delivery-day vlog shared online, Divyanka had been candid about her nerves. "Yaar thoda sa anxious hoon," she admitted. "It felt like an exam. Jab tak ho nahi jae tab tak sukoon nahin." Doctors were monitoring the twins' heartbeat and movement, and every dip in motion triggered a wave of worry.

## A Decade in the Making

For fans who have followed Divyanka since her breakout role as Dr. Ishita in Yeh Hai Mohabbatein — one of Indian television's longest-running and most beloved serials — the twins represent a long-awaited chapter. The couple married in 2016 and had spoken openly about wanting children, while also fielding the constant public questioning that Indian couples, especially women, face about parenthood timelines.

In the diaspora, where Divyanka's shows are widely streamed and she remains one of the most recognized Indian television faces, the response has been overwhelmingly warm. Social media timelines in NRI communities filled with congratulatory messages, baby shower gift ideas, and nostalgic clips from Yeh Hai Mohabbatein.

## Privacy in the Age of Paparazzi

The couple's decision to request face privacy for their twins is notable in an industry where celebrity baby reveals have become a content genre of their own. Katrina Kaif and Vicky Kaushal recently introduced their baby Vihaan to Mumbai's paparazzi but with a similar rule: controlled, brief, and on their terms.

Divyanka's approach — showing her baby to the watchman but asking cameras to look away — captures a tension that NRI audiences understand well: the desire to share joy within your community while maintaining boundaries with the wider world.

For now, the Dahiya household is adjusting to life with two newborns, and Divyanka's Instagram has gone quiet. That silence, for once, is the happiest kind.
author: Diaspora Desk
